- SOLO = 1 location, GROWTH = up to 3, FRANCHISE = 4+.

- PesaPal is LIVE for owner SaaS billing only.

- `support:session:read|write`

The same token therefore exercises every folder.

description.content:
**Audience:** owner.

**Why:** demonstrates location-only downgrade enforcement. SOLO allows exactly 1 active location — if the org currently has more, this returns 409 with a `violations` payload citing the location count.

**Real-world example:** GROWTH customer with 2 branches tries to downgrade to SOLO — they must close or transfer one branch first.

**Audience:** owner.

**Why:** demonstrates the reversible part of the lifecycle. SUSPENDED can be flipped back to ACTIVE at any time, so this collection stays runnable end-to-end. The terminal CANCELLED transition is intentionally NOT exercised here — running it would block every downstream create (`Subscription is cancelled. Cannot create resources.`). Operators wanting to test cancellation can manually PATCH `{ status: 'CANCELLED', cancelReason: '...' }`.

**Real-world example:** PesaPal payment failed past the grace period — Nimbus suspends the org until they retry the SaaS checkout.

**Audience:** owner / Nimbus support.

**Why:** reverses the previous SUSPENDED transition so subsequent folders (developer portal, support sessions, ops admin) can run cleanly without `Subscription is cancelled. Cannot create resources.` errors.

**LIVE.** This is the only live PesaPal flow in the repo. Owners pay Nimbus for their SaaS subscription. The flow:

1. `POST /billing/pesapal/checkout-session` → returns a redirect URL to PesaPal-hosted payment page and an `orderTrackingId`.
2. Customer completes payment on PesaPal.
3. `GET /billing/pesapal/callback` is called by PesaPal in the customer's browser.
4. `POST /billing/pesapal/ipn` is called server-to-server by PesaPal.
5. `POST /billing/pesapal/reconcile-status` lets ops force-poll PesaPal if a callback / IPN is delayed.

Nimbus stores only safe payment references (`orderTrackingId`, `merchantReference`, `status`) and never raw card data. Subscription transitions to ACTIVE only after a verified COMPLETED status.

**Audience:** owner.

**Why:** the entry point of every SaaS payment. Returns the PesaPal redirect URL; the owner is sent there to enter card / mobile-money details on PesaPal's hosted page. Re-running with an already-INITIATED transaction auto-cancels the old one and starts a fresh session.

**Real-world example:** owner clicks 'Pay now' on the upgrade screen.

**Env vars required on the server:** `PESAPAL_CONSUMER_KEY`, `PESAPAL_CONSUMER_SECRET`, `PESAPAL_BASE_URL`, `PESAPAL_IPN_CALLBACK_URL`. Without them, the endpoint returns 500.

info.name: M39.1 — Commercial Foundation + SaaS Billing + Developer Portal

description.content:
## What this collection covers

M39.1 is the **commercial and platform-control foundation** of Nimbus.

It fully owns:

- **Plan catalog** — SOLO / GROWTH / FRANCHISE only.
- **Pricing (locked):** SOLO USD 80/mo (864/yr), GROWTH USD 150/mo (1620/yr), FRANCHISE USD 200/mo (2160/yr) — annual ≈ 10% discount.
- **Subscription lifecycle** — PENDING_PAYMENT → ACTIVE → GRACE_PERIOD / PAST_DUE / SUSPENDED / CANCELLED, plus monthly ↔ annual and solo ↔ growth ↔ franchise transitions.
- **Location-only enforcement** — the only commercial cap on plans is location count. There is **no feature gating**. Every plan grants the full Nimbus feature set (POS, KDS, inventory, accounting, HR, reporting, analytics, reservations, events, developer portal, franchise / HQ analytics).
- **PesaPal SaaS billing — LIVE** for restaurant owners paying Nimbus subscriptions. This is the only live PesaPal flow in the repo. Owners pay Nimbus; restaurants do NOT take diner payments through this flow.
- **Developer portal** — full-access integration API keys, outbound webhooks, usage with location-cap context, protected dev-admin listing.
- **Support-session foundation** — owner-facing.
- **Internal plan-catalog admin** — Nimbus internal admins manage prices / caps / status without redeploys.

## What M39.1 does NOT own

- Public commerce (restaurants, events, holds) — kept where the M39 reconstruction left it; will move under M39.2+.
- Merchant payment connectivity (mobile money) — pending and labelled NOT LIVE.
- Public-side diner payments — pending and labelled NOT LIVE.

## Audiences

- **Owner** — restaurant owner using the SaaS.
- **Developer** — owner-side or trusted vendor consuming the developer portal.
- **Nimbus Internal Admin** — Nimbus ops staff managing the SaaS plan catalog.

## Folder structure

1. `00 Read Me` — orientation only.
2. `A. Auth` — login as owner.
3. `B. Plan Catalog & Billing Overview` — public plans, billing-side plans, billing overview with locationCapacity.
4. `C. Subscription Change (location-only enforcement)` — change plans + billing cycle; verifies location-only enforcement.
5. `D. SaaS Billing via PesaPal` — checkout-session, callback, IPN, reconcile-status (LIVE).
6. `E. Developer Portal` — API keys, webhooks, usage (location-led), dev-admins.
7. `F. Support Sessions` — owner-facing open / list / close.
8. `G. Ops Plan Catalog Admin` — Nimbus-internal CRUD on the plan catalog.

## Postman conventions

- `accessToken` is auto-captured by `A. Auth → Login (owner)`.
- All authenticated requests send `Authorization: Bearer {{accessToken}}`.
- PesaPal `callback` and `ipn` requests are public (no auth header) — they are reached by PesaPal, not the owner.
- Login is asserted as 200 OR 201 because Nest's default for POST is 201 while the auth controller may return 200 in some builds; both are acceptable as long as `accessToken` is set.
